question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

He was so enraged at the article about him that he sued the newspaper.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Angered.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Enraged" means made very angry / furious. Its closest synonym is "Angered". (अत्यधिक क्रोधित)

◦ Correct: He was so enraged (angered) at the article about him that he sued the newspaper.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Generated" (produced/created), Option 2 "Determined" (resolved/decided) and Option 4 "Enhanced" (improved) are unrelated to anger.

NOTE

• Synonyms of enraged: angered, infuriated, incensed, furious, irate. Antonyms: pleased, calmed, delighted, soothed.

question:
Recognise the sentence with the correct transitive verb form of break.

A. The cyclone broke the window.  B. The window broke.  C. The cyclone caused the breaking of window.  D. The cyclone caused the broken window.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. A — "The cyclone broke the window."

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A transitive verb is one that takes a direct object (it acts upon something). In sentence A, "broke" is followed by the object "the window" — "The cyclone broke the window" — so "break" is used correctly as a transitive verb.

◦ Structure: Subject (cyclone) + transitive verb (broke) + object (the window).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• In sentence B ("The window broke"), "broke" has no object — here it is intransitive, not transitive.

• Sentences C and D avoid the finite verb altogether, using the noun "breaking" or the adjective "broken", so neither shows the transitive verb "break".

NOTE

• "Break" is both transitive (He broke the glass) and intransitive (The glass broke). A transitive verb always answers "broke what?" with an object.

question:
Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

BBC Media has shown exponenteal growth in their revenue this year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. exponenteal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Exponenteal" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "exponential", meaning very rapid (growth) that increases more and more quickly. (तीव्र गति से बढ़ना)

◦ Correct: BBC Media has shown exponential growth in their revenue this year.

• Spelling key: EX + PO + NEN + TIAL.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "revenue" (income), "media" and "year" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: exponent, exponentially. "Exponential growth" describes a doubling/compounding increase (as in the powers of a number).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Leisure activities are activities that people ___________ in during their free time while they are not working.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. engage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal expression "engage in" means to take part in / be involved in an activity. So people "engage in" leisure activities during their free time. (भाग लेना)

◦ Correct: ... activities that people engage in during their free time ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "encourage" (to give support), Option 3 "evaluate" (to assess) and Option 4 "exempt" (to free from an obligation) do not collocate with "in" to give this meaning.

NOTE

• "Engage in (an activity)" = participate in it. Also note "engaged to" (to be married), "engaged with" (occupied with).

question: Select the option that has used the correct tense.
option_1: By the time we arrive at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
option_2: By the time we arrived at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
option_3: By the time we arrives at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
option_4: By the time we arriving at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. By the time we arrived at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When one past action is completed before another past action, we use the past simple for the later event and the past perfect (continuous) for the earlier, longer one. "By the time we arrived (past simple) ... they had been waiting (past perfect continuous) for over an hour."

◦ Correct: By the time we arrived at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "arrive" and Option 3 "arrives" are present-tense forms and clash with the past "had been waiting".

• Option 4 "arriving" is a non-finite form and cannot stand as the main verb of the clause.

NOTE

• Past perfect continuous = had + been + V-ing, used for an action going on up to a point in the past (had been waiting for an hour).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

It is a common perception / that the rich sometimes / despise poor.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. despise poor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When an adjective denotes a class of people (rich, poor, blind, etc.), it must be preceded by "the" and functions as a plural noun. Since "the rich" is used earlier, the parallel form is "the poor", not just "poor".

◦ Correct: ... that the rich sometimes despise the poor.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "It is a common perception" and "that the rich sometimes" are grammatically correct.

NOTE

• "The + adjective" = a whole class/group: the rich, the poor, the young, the elderly, the unemployed. These take a plural verb (The poor are ...).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Searing
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Freezing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Searing" means extremely hot / burning (scorching). Its antonym is "Freezing", meaning extremely cold. (झुलसा देने वाला का विलोम — अत्यधिक ठंडा)

◦ Example: The searing desert heat was the opposite of the freezing mountain air.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Mocking" (ridiculing), Option 2 "Pressing" (urgent) and Option 4 "Thrilling" (exciting) are unrelated to temperature.

NOTE

• Synonyms of searing: scorching, blistering, burning, sweltering. Antonyms: freezing, icy, frosty, chilly.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Prem is an excellent chess player. He is the _______ student of the class too.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. most intelligent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" before the blank and the phrase "of the class" (a comparison among the whole group) call for the superlative degree — "the most intelligent".

◦ Correct: He is the most intelligent student of the class too.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "more intelligent" is the comparative (used with "than", between two), which does not fit "the ... of the class".

• Option 2 "intelligently" is an adverb and Option 3 "intelligent" (positive degree) do not suit "the ... student of the class".

NOTE

• Degrees: intelligent – more intelligent (than) – the most intelligent (of/in a group). Use the superlative with "the" when comparing one with all others.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Boisterous
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Quiet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Boisterous" means noisy, rowdy and full of energy. Its antonym is "Quiet", meaning calm and making little noise. (कोलाहलपूर्ण का विलोम — शांत)

◦ Example: The boisterous crowd fell quiet when the anthem began.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Noisy" is a synonym of boisterous.

• Option 2 "Benevolent" (kind) and Option 3 "Buoyant" (cheerful/floating) are unrelated antonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of boisterous: noisy, rowdy, unruly, loud, exuberant. Antonyms: quiet, calm, restrained, subdued.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the highlighted group of words in the given sentence.

The minister went to visit the monuments set up for people who were buried in other countries.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. cenotaphs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "cenotaph" is a monument (tomb-like structure) built in honour of a person or people whose remains are buried elsewhere / in another place. It exactly matches "monuments set up for people who were buried in other countries". (स्मारक — जहाँ शव कहीं और दफ़न हो)

◦ Example: The cenotaph honours soldiers buried far from home.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "graves" (holes where bodies are buried), Option 2 "cemetery" (a burial ground) and Option 4 "coffins" (boxes for a dead body) all involve the actual body, unlike a cenotaph.

NOTE

• Root: Greek "kenos" (empty) + "taphos" (tomb) → an "empty tomb". India Gate in Delhi is a famous cenotaph honouring fallen soldiers.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Sushil, who recently joined our school / was awarded the Gold Cup / as he worked hardly / throughout the year.
option_2: Sushil, who recently joined our school
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. as he worked hardly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hardly" is NOT the adverb form of "hard"; it means "scarcely / almost not". The intended meaning is that he worked with effort, for which the correct word is "hard" (which is both an adjective and an adverb).

◦ Correct: ... as he worked hard throughout the year.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Sushil, who recently joined our school", "was awarded the Gold Cup" and "throughout the year" are all correct.

NOTE

• "He works hard" (with effort) vs "He hardly works" (almost never). Similar traps: late/lately, near/nearly, high/highly.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

His sudden resignation left the company in a very difficult situation and to have to make a hard decision as they scrambled to find a replacement.
option_3: between a rock and a hard place
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. between a rock and a hard place.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "between a rock and a hard place" means in a very difficult situation where one has to choose between two equally unpleasant options. It fits "a very difficult situation ... make a hard decision". (दो कठिनाइयों के बीच फँसना)

◦ Example: With both choices costly, the board was between a rock and a hard place.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "in the dark" (unaware), Option 2 "with a silver lining" (a hopeful side of a bad situation) and Option 4 "on cloud nine" (extremely happy) do not fit a difficult dilemma.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of dilemma: "caught between two stools", "in a fix", "on the horns of a dilemma", "in a tight spot".

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The weather was absolutley perfect for the outdoor event.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. absolutely.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "absolutely", meaning completely / totally. (पूर्णतः)

◦ Correct: The weather was absolutely perfect for the outdoor event.

• Spelling key: AB + SO + LUTE + LY (from "absolute" + "-ly").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspelt: "absoultely", "absoluttley" and "absolutly" all disturb the base word "absolute".

NOTE

• To form the adverb, add "-ly" to "absolute" → keep the full base and simply attach "-ly": absolute → absolutely.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

an open book
option_1: someone who gives advice based on theory not practice
option_3: a person of whom her mother is extremely proud
option_4: a person or thing that is easy to learn about and understand
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. a person or thing that is easy to learn about and understand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "an open book" refers to a person (or thing) whose thoughts, feelings or nature are easy to know and understand — nothing is hidden. (खुली किताब — जिसे आसानी से समझा जा सके)

◦ Example: You always know how she feels; she is an open book.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 describe an armchair theorist, a helpful person and a favoured child respectively — none matches "an open book".

NOTE

• Opposite idea: "a closed book" = something/someone difficult to understand, as in "He is a closed book about his past".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Meticulous
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Regardless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Meticulous" means very careful, precise and attentive to every small detail. Its antonym is "Regardless" (here meaning careless / paying no heed / without attention to detail). (सूक्ष्म/सतर्क का विलोम — लापरवाह)

◦ Example: A meticulous worker checks everything, whereas a regardless (careless) worker ignores details.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Persevering" (persistent), Option 2 "Exemplary" (model/ideal) and Option 3 "Determined" (resolute) are broadly positive and do not oppose "meticulous".

NOTE

• Synonyms of meticulous: careful, thorough, scrupulous, painstaking. Antonyms: careless, sloppy, negligent, slapdash.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

I have never seen so beautiful a landscape than this one.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. than this one.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "so + adjective + a/an + noun ... as" takes "as", not "than". "Than" is used only with the comparative degree, but here there is no comparative. So it should be "as this one".

◦ Correct: I have never seen so beautiful a landscape as this one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "I have never seen", "so beautiful" and "a landscape" are all correct in this construction ("so + adjective + a + singular noun").

NOTE

• "As ... as" is used for equality/positive degree; "than" only with comparatives (bigger than, more beautiful than). "So beautiful a landscape as" is correct.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A post without any remuneration
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Honorary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Honorary" describes a post/position held without any salary or payment (remuneration) — held as an honour. (अवैतनिक / मानद पद)

◦ Example: She serves as the honorary secretary of the club, receiving no pay.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Illegible" (unable to be read), Option 2 "Bigot" (an intolerant person) and Option 3 "Effeminate" (having womanly qualities) do not relate to an unpaid post.

NOTE

• Related: "honorary degree" (given as an honour, without study). Do not confuse with "honorable" (deserving respect).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Corroborate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Support.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Corroborate" means to confirm or give supporting evidence for a statement/theory. Its closest synonym is "Support". (पुष्टि करना / समर्थन करना)

◦ Example: The witness's account corroborated (supported) the victim's story.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Suggest" (to propose), Option 3 "Contend" (to argue/assert or compete) and Option 4 "Elaborate" (to explain in detail) do not mean to confirm with evidence.

NOTE

• Synonyms of corroborate: confirm, verify, substantiate, validate, endorse. Antonyms: contradict, refute, disprove.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase.

Belonging or pertaining to an individual from birth
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Congenital.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Congenital" means existing from or present at birth (especially of a trait or a disease). It matches "belonging ... to an individual from birth". (जन्मजात)

◦ Example: A congenital heart defect is one present from birth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Congregational" (relating to a congregation/assembly), Option 3 "Congruent" (in agreement / matching) and Option 4 "Congenial" (friendly/pleasant) do not mean "from birth".

NOTE

• "Congenital" (from birth) vs "genetic" (inherited through genes) vs "hereditary" (passed from parents). Congenital conditions may or may not be inherited.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Forgetfull.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Forgetfull" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "forgetful", meaning tending to forget things. The suffix "-ful" is always written with a single 'l'. (भुलक्कड़)

◦ Correct: My grandfather has become quite forgetful.

• Spelling key: FORGET + FUL (one 'l').

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Damaged", "Fantastic" and "Expensive" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• The suffix "-ful" always has one 'l': beautiful, careful, useful, helpful, forgetful. (It doubles to "-fully" only when "-ly" is added: carefully.)

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Though people are becoming health-conscious these days, (1)________ simple lifestyle habits they are prone to fatal diseases. (2)________ a new study published in 'The Journal of the American College of Cardiology', (3)________ food more sparingly is linked to a lower risk of heart disease, heart failure , and ischemic heart disease. A significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, is demonstrated to be correlated (4)________ high sodium intake. As per the research, a person's individual sodium intake over time may be predicted by how (5)____ they salt their food. It is found that people who do not put a little additional salt to their food very often had a much lower risk of heart disease event regardless of lifestyle factors and pre-existing disease.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. because of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Because of" is a prepositional phrase followed by a noun/noun phrase ("simple lifestyle habits"). It gives the reason — people fall ill because of their simple/poor lifestyle habits. (के कारण)

◦ Correct: ... because of simple lifestyle habits they are prone to fatal diseases.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "because" is a conjunction and must be followed by a clause (subject + verb), not just a noun phrase.

• Option 1 "for" and Option 4 "but" do not give the cause-and-effect link needed here.

NOTE

• "Because" + clause (because they neglect habits); "because of" + noun (because of habits). Both mean "for the reason that".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Though people are becoming health-conscious these days, (1)________ simple lifestyle habits they are prone to fatal diseases. (2)________ a new study published in 'The Journal of the American College of Cardiology', (3)________ food more sparingly is linked to a lower risk of heart disease, heart failure , and ischemic heart disease. A significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, is demonstrated to be correlated (4)________ high sodium intake. As per the research, a person's individual sodium intake over time may be predicted by how (5)____ they salt their food. It is found that people who do not put a little additional salt to their food very often had a much lower risk of heart disease event regardless of lifestyle factors and pre-existing disease.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. According to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression "according to" is used to cite a source or authority ("a new study ..."). It means "as stated by". (के अनुसार)

◦ Correct: According to a new study published in 'The Journal of the American College of Cardiology' ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "According with", Option 3 "In according with" are ungrammatical.

• Option 2 "Accordingly" is an adverb meaning "therefore / in a corresponding way" and cannot introduce a source.

NOTE

• Remember: it is always "according to (someone/something)" — never "according with". "According to me" reports one's opinion.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Though people are becoming health-conscious these days, (1)________ simple lifestyle habits they are prone to fatal diseases. (2)________ a new study published in 'The Journal of the American College of Cardiology', (3)________ food more sparingly is linked to a lower risk of heart disease, heart failure , and ischemic heart disease. A significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, is demonstrated to be correlated (4)________ high sodium intake. As per the research, a person's individual sodium intake over time may be predicted by how (5)____ they salt their food. It is found that people who do not put a little additional salt to their food very often had a much lower risk of heart disease event regardless of lifestyle factors and pre-existing disease.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. salting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a gerund (V-ing) to act as the subject of the verb "is linked". "Salting food more sparingly is linked to a lower risk ..." — the "-ing" form works as a noun (subject). (क्रिया का संज्ञा-रूप)

◦ Correct: ... salting food more sparingly is linked to a lower risk of heart disease ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "salt" (base verb) and Option 2 "salted" (past form) cannot function as the subject of the sentence.

• Option 4 "salt with" is grammatically wrong here.

NOTE

• A gerund (V-ing used as a noun) can be the subject of a sentence: "Reading is fun", "Salting food ... is linked ...". The verb that follows is singular.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Though people are becoming health-conscious these days, (1)________ simple lifestyle habits they are prone to fatal diseases. (2)________ a new study published in 'The Journal of the American College of Cardiology', (3)________ food more sparingly is linked to a lower risk of heart disease, heart failure , and ischemic heart disease. A significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, is demonstrated to be correlated (4)________ high sodium intake. As per the research, a person's individual sodium intake over time may be predicted by how (5)____ they salt their food. It is found that people who do not put a little additional salt to their food very often had a much lower risk of heart disease event regardless of lifestyle factors and pre-existing disease.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "correlate" takes the preposition "with". High blood pressure is "correlated with high sodium intake" — i.e., the two are connected/associated. (के साथ संबंधित)

◦ Correct: ... high blood pressure, is demonstrated to be correlated with high sodium intake.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Prepositions "in", "of" and "for" do not collocate with "correlated" in standard usage.

NOTE

• Fixed collocations: "correlated with", "associated with", "linked to/with", "connected with/to". Note earlier the passage uses "linked to".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Though people are becoming health-conscious these days, (1)________ simple lifestyle habits they are prone to fatal diseases. (2)________ a new study published in 'The Journal of the American College of Cardiology', (3)________ food more sparingly is linked to a lower risk of heart disease, heart failure , and ischemic heart disease. A significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, is demonstrated to be correlated (4)________ high sodium intake. As per the research, a person's individual sodium intake over time may be predicted by how (5)____ they salt their food. It is found that people who do not put a little additional salt to their food very often had a much lower risk of heart disease event regardless of lifestyle factors and pre-existing disease.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. frequently.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs an adverb of frequency to modify "they salt their food". "How frequently they salt their food" (i.e., how often) fits the context of measuring salt intake over time. (कितनी बार / अक्सर)

◦ Correct: ... may be predicted by how frequently they salt their food.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "soundly" (deeply/thoroughly, as in sleep), Option 2 "hefty" (large/heavy) and Option 3 "burly" (strong and heavily built) are adjectives/adverbs that do not describe how often something is done.

• The passage's last line ("... do not put a little additional salt ... very often") confirms the theme of frequency.

NOTE

• Adverbs of frequency: always, usually, often, frequently, sometimes, rarely, never. They tell "how often" an action happens.
